--[[
	Bootstrap  -  Part-Icles V5 ShortcutKey wiring entry point
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle

	Mirrors Randomizer/Bootstrap.luau.

	Order of operations:
	  1. Build ShortcutsWiring state machine, register ctx.ShortcutsWiring.
	  2. wiring.ensureSettings()  -  primes _settings with the user's saved bindings
	     (or empty on a fresh install) BEFORE Runtime.start, so the dispatcher's
	     first index rebuild has data.
	  3. Shortcuts.Runtime.start  -  UIS dispatcher hooks wiring.setOnChanged for live
	     index rebuilds; registers via ConnectionManager so plugin teardown disconnects
	     cleanly.
	  4. Settings panel "Shortcuts" button → toggle wiring.open/close.
	  5. Panel headerCloseBtn (built-in W.makeToolPanel Hd.Close) → close().

	Required deps shape:
	  ctx (must contain ctx.plugin + ctx.Actions),
	  UI (must contain ShortcutPanel + ShortcutsList + ShortcutsSearch + ShortcutsReset
	      + ShortcutsHeaderClose + ShortcutsButton on Settings panel),
	  Connections (ConnectionManager  -  same instance used by init.server.lua),
	  Shortcuts (the barrel; needs Bindings + Wiring + Runtime),
	  Widgets, Theme.
]]

local Bootstrap = {}

function Bootstrap.attach(deps)
	local ctx = deps.ctx
	local UI = deps.UI
	local Connections = deps.Connections
	local Shortcuts = deps.Shortcuts

	local wiring = Shortcuts.Wiring({
		ctx = ctx,
		panel = {
			panel = UI.ShortcutPanel,
			scrollList = UI.ShortcutsList,
			searchBox = UI.ShortcutsSearch,
			resetBtn = UI.ShortcutsReset,
			headerCloseBtn = UI.ShortcutsHeaderClose,
			leaderLabel = UI.ShortcutsLeaderLabel,
			leaderSetBtn = UI.ShortcutsLeaderSet,
			leaderClearBtn = UI.ShortcutsLeaderClear,
		},
		Bindings = Shortcuts.Bindings,
		-- Forward Connections so search/reset signals register through the shared
		-- ConnectionManager (consistent with every other top-level wiring path).
		Connections = Connections,
		Widgets = deps.Widgets,
		Theme = deps.Theme,
	})
	ctx.ShortcutsWiring = wiring

	-- Prime _settings at setup so the runtime (which attaches below) sees the user's
	-- saved bindings (or empty fresh install) on first dispatch.
	wiring.ensureSettings()

	-- Shared dispatcher with 50ms dedup. Runtime is currently the only live caller  - 
	-- dedup is retained as future-proofing for any new dispatch path that gets added.
	-- Built BEFORE Runtime.start so it can hook in.
	local dispatcher = Shortcuts.Dispatcher.create(ctx)
	ctx.ShortcutsDispatcher = dispatcher

	-- Start the UIS dispatcher. wiring.setOnChanged is hooked inside Runtime.start so
	-- any save-side rebuild flows through. ctx.ShortcutsRuntime exposed for teardown
	-- (plugin Unloading -> stop()) and future debug introspection.
	local runtime = Shortcuts.Runtime.start({
		ctx = ctx,
		wiring = wiring,
		Bindings = Shortcuts.Bindings,
		Connections = Connections,
		dispatcher = dispatcher,
		workspacesLabel = UI.WorkspacesLabel,
	})
	ctx.ShortcutsRuntime = runtime

	-- PluginActions.register is a disabled no-op under the P-prefix leader policy.
	-- The call is kept (returns {stop = function() end}) so we don't have to wire
	-- conditional code paths if the policy ever flips back. See PluginActions.luau
	-- header for the bypass rationale.
	if ctx.plugin then
		ctx.ShortcutsPluginActions = Shortcuts.PluginActions.register(ctx.plugin, ctx, wiring, dispatcher)
	end

	-- Settings panel "Shortcuts" button. Toggle behaviour: open if closed, close if open.
	if UI.ShortcutsButton then
		Connections["ShortcutsToggle"] = UI.ShortcutsButton.Activated:Connect(function()
			if wiring.isOpen() then wiring.close() else wiring.open() end
		end)
	end

	-- Built-in W.makeToolPanel header X. close() so capture connection tears down.
	if UI.ShortcutsHeaderClose then
		Connections["ShortcutsHeaderClose"] = UI.ShortcutsHeaderClose.Activated:Connect(function()
			wiring.close()
		end)
	end

	return wiring
end

return Bootstrap

--[[
	Dispatcher  -  Part-Icles V5 ShortcutKey shared dispatch
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle

	The only live dispatch path is `UIS InputBegan -> Runtime overlay reverse-index
	match -> handler`. Single dispatch chokepoint is preserved as future-proofing:
	any new path that gets added calls `Dispatcher.dispatch(actionId)` and inherits
	the 50ms dedup discipline.

	Two dedup layers  -  kept because Runtime can still fire twice if an InputBegan
	repeat slips through the focus gates:
	  - `_lastFire[actionId] -> os.clock()` per-action 50ms window. Catches same-action
	    double dispatch.
	  - `_lastAnyFire -> os.clock()` global 50ms window. Catches cross-action collisions
	     -  future-proofing for any additional dispatch path.

	The `def.implemented == true` guard also runs here so callers can drop their own
	duplicate checks (kept defensively at the caller in case dispatcher is bypassed).

	Lifecycle:
	  Dispatcher.create(ctx) returns `{dispatch}`. Stored on `ctx.ShortcutsDispatcher`
	  by Bootstrap. No teardown needed  -  `_lastFire` + `_lastAnyFire` are scoped per
	  Dispatcher instance and GC'd when ctx is dropped.

	NOT user-script-reachable. Internal-only.
]]

local Log = require(script.Parent.Parent.Part.Log)

local Dispatcher = {}

local DEDUP_WINDOW = 0.05  -- 50ms; matches Runtime's prior per-instance dedup

function Dispatcher.create(ctx)
	local self = {}
	local _lastFire = {}      -- per-actionId: same chord on overlay+Studio doesn't double-fire.
	-- Initialize to nil + guarded check so the very first dispatch in a fresh context
	-- isn't suppressed when os.clock() happens to be below DEDUP_WINDOW. Could also
	-- use -math.huge; nil reads cleaner.
	local _lastAnyFire = nil  -- global cross-action dedup window.

	function self.dispatch(actionId)
		if type(actionId) ~= "string" or actionId == "" then return end
		local Actions = ctx.Actions
		local def = Actions and Actions[actionId]
		-- Second-guard applied centrally: even if a caller bypasses its own implemented
		-- check, the dispatcher refuses stub actions.
		if not def or def.implemented ~= true then return end
		local now = os.clock()
		local last = _lastFire[actionId]
		if last and (now - last) < DEDUP_WINDOW then return end
		if _lastAnyFire and (now - _lastAnyFire) < DEDUP_WINDOW then return end
		_lastFire[actionId] = now
		_lastAnyFire = now
		local ok, err = pcall(def.handler, ctx)
		if not ok then
			Log.warn(("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] handler error for %q: %s"):format(actionId, tostring(err)))
		end
	end

	return self
end

return Dispatcher

--[[
	PluginActions  -  DISABLED under the P-prefix leader policy
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle

	Empty stub. Studio `PluginAction` registration was the original mechanism for
	surfacing plugin shortcuts in Studio's File → Advanced → Customize Shortcuts
	dialog. The hold-P leader policy ("all keybinds require P first") makes that
	mechanism unsafe because Studio cannot prove the user pressed our leader key
	before firing `PluginAction.Triggered`  -  Studio-bound chords would end-run the
	policy.

	The previous body created `PluginAction`s with `allowBinding = true` and hooked
	their `Triggered` signal through the shared dispatcher. That entire path is
	deliberately deleted here so a future careless edit cannot re-enable the bypass
	by calling a "legacy" function. The stub keeps the same call signature so
	Bootstrap doesn't have to know whether the policy is active.

	Side effect: `PluginAction` instances created by older plugin versions may still
	appear in Studio's Customize Shortcuts dialog with stale bindings. Those bindings
	cannot fire because we no longer connect Triggered. Users can clear them via the
	dialog at their leisure  -  the plugin cannot mutate Studio's binding store.

	NOT user-script-reachable. Internal-only.
]]

local PluginActions = {}

function PluginActions.register(_plugin, _ctx, _wiring, _dispatcher)
	return {stop = function() end}
end

return PluginActions

--[[
	Runtime  -  Part-Icles V5 ShortcutKey UIS dispatch
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle

	Connects keyboard chords to ActionCatalog handlers via a comboKey reverse-index
	built from `wiring.getSettings()`.

	**Hold-P leader:**
	All shortcuts require P held down at the moment of the chord keypress. Roblox
	Studio uses heavy modifier prefixes (Ctrl/Shift/Alt) for its own shortcuts, so a
	dedicated leader key sidesteps that whole conflict surface. Hold-style (vs.
	tap-once + 1s window) lets the user hold P and tap multiple keys to fire several
	actions in a row without re-pressing P each time.

	Sequence:
	  1. User holds P down. P alone fires nothing (P is the modifier, not an action).
	  2. While P is still held, any other keypress builds a combo and dispatches if
	     its comboKey hits the reverse-index. User can tap several chord keys in
	     succession.
	  3. User releases P → leader off. Next chord key without P held is ignored.

	Architecture:
	  - Reverse-index `_index[comboKey] -> actionId` rebuilt on demand AND whenever
	    the Wiring layer fires its onChanged callback (after every save: commit /
	    unbind / reset).
	  - 50ms per-actionId dedup + global cross-action dedup live in
	    Shortcuts.Dispatcher.
	  - Focus gating:
	      1. `wiring.isCapturing()` → skip (panel actively capturing a chord).
	      2. `UserInputService:GetFocusedTextBox()` → skip (let typing pass through
	         to the focused text input  -  overlay shortcuts must NOT eat keystrokes
	         from properties / search / config inputs).
	      3. `wiring.isOpen()` → SUPPRESS but allow `ToggleShortcuts` and `ToggleUI`
	         through: the same shortcut that opened the panel must be able to close
	         it, and ToggleUI must work when the panel is open under a hidden
	         ScreenGui. Other actions are blocked so chord-tapping during binding
	         doesn't fire random actions.
	    The `gameProcessedEvent` gate is intentionally NOT used because Studio sets
	    it true for nearly every keyboard event.

	Direct actions (`direct = true` in the catalog: the workspace keys) are not dispatched
	here. Their bindings go to Shortcuts/WorkspaceKeys on start and after every save;
	Modules/Workspaces reads them from its own listener, which outlives this runtime.

	Required deps shape:
	  ctx (must contain ctx.Actions),
	  wiring (needs getSettings + isOpen + isCapturing + captureHoldsKeys + setOnChanged),
	  workspacesLabel (optional TextLabel: the Settings panel's Workspaces row),
	  Bindings (for comboKey + isValidCombo),
	  Connections (ConnectionManager),
	  dispatcher (Shortcuts.Dispatcher.create(ctx)).

	NOT user-script-reachable. Internal-only.
]]

local Log = require(script.Parent.Parent.Part.Log)
local WorkspaceKeys = require(script.Parent.WorkspaceKeys)

local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

-- The keys the Settings panel's Workspaces row names, by their WorkspaceKeys name.
local WORKSPACE_ROW_KEYS = { "next", "new", "merge" }

-- Leader is now user-configurable via Settings (Bindings.leaderKey). Defaults to P
-- so existing users see no behavior change on upgrade. A leader of `false` skips
-- the gate entirely; chord combos fire on direct keypress.
local DEFAULT_LEADER_KEYCODE = Enum.KeyCode.P

local Runtime = {}

function Runtime.start(deps)
	local ctx = deps.ctx
	local wiring = deps.wiring
	local Bindings = deps.Bindings
	local Connections = deps.Connections
	local dispatcher = deps.dispatcher

	local runtime = {}
	local _index = {}        -- comboKey -> actionId

	function runtime._rebuildIndex()
		_index = {}
		local settings = wiring.getSettings()
		if not settings or settings.overlayEnabled == false then return end
		local Actions = ctx.Actions
		for actionId, combo in pairs(settings.bindings or {}) do
			local def = Actions and Actions[actionId]
			-- Index-build filter: stubs skipped here so a malformed config doesn't
			-- even land in _index. Dispatcher repeats the check defensively at fire
			-- time in case bypass paths land.
			if def and def.implemented == true and not def.direct and Bindings.isValidCombo(combo) then
				_index[Bindings.comboKey(combo)] = actionId
			end
		end
	end

	-- Hands the workspace keys to Shortcuts/WorkspaceKeys and names them on the Settings row.
	function runtime._pushWorkspaceKeys()
		local settings = wiring.getSettings()
		if not settings then
			return
		end
		local combos = {}
		for actionId, def in pairs(ctx.Actions or {}) do
			local combo = settings.bindings[actionId]
			if def.workspaceKey and combo and Bindings.isValidCombo(combo) then
				combos[def.workspaceKey] = combo
			end
		end
		WorkspaceKeys.set(combos, Bindings.getLeaderKey(settings))

		local rowLabel = deps.workspacesLabel
		if not rowLabel then
			return
		end
		local names = {}
		for _, workspaceKey in ipairs(WORKSPACE_ROW_KEYS) do
			if combos[workspaceKey] then
				table.insert(names, Bindings.formatCombo(combos[workspaceKey], false, false))
			end
		end
		if #names > 0 then
			rowLabel.Text = "Workspaces ( " .. table.concat(names, "  ") .. " )"
		else
			rowLabel.Text = "Workspaces"
		end
	end

	-- Build a combo table from a keyboard InputObject. Mirrors Wiring's capture-side combo
	-- construction so the comboKey hash matches between save-time and dispatch-time.
	local function _buildComboFromInput(input)
		local combo = {
			key = input.KeyCode.Name,
			ctrl = UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.LeftControl) or UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.RightControl),
			alt = UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.LeftAlt) or UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.RightAlt),
			shift = UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift) or UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.RightShift),
			meta = false,
		}
		pcall(function()
			combo.meta = UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.LeftMeta) or UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.RightMeta)
		end)
		return combo
	end

	-- Resolve the live leader KeyCode from settings on each check. Settings table is
	-- in-memory after first ensureSettings, so the lookup is cheap. Returns the
	-- KeyCode enum value OR nil when leader is disabled (false in settings).
	local function _currentLeaderKeyCode()
		local settings = wiring.getSettings()
		local lk = Bindings.getLeaderKey(settings)
		if lk == false then return nil end
		local ok, kc = pcall(function() return Enum.KeyCode[lk] end)
		if ok and kc then return kc end
		return DEFAULT_LEADER_KEYCODE
	end

	-- Hold-leader: dispatch fires on any second-key press WHILE the leader is held.
	-- Lets the user hold the leader and tap multiple keys to toggle several actions
	-- in a row without re-arming each time. When leader is disabled (settings.leaderKey
	-- == false), this returns true unconditionally so chords fire on direct keypress.
	local function _isLeaderHeld()
		local kc = _currentLeaderKeyCode()
		if kc == nil then return true end
		return UserInputService:IsKeyDown(kc)
	end

	local function _dispatchActionId(actionId)
		if not actionId then return end
		if dispatcher then
			dispatcher.dispatch(actionId)
			return
		end
		-- Defensive fallback if Bootstrap forgot to wire dispatcher.
		Log.warn("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] Runtime built without dispatcher; firing direct (dedup absent)")
		local def = ctx.Actions and ctx.Actions[actionId]
		if def and def.implemented == true then
			local ok, err = pcall(def.handler, ctx)
			if not ok then
				Log.warn(("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] handler error for %q: %s"):format(actionId, tostring(err)))
			end
		end
	end

	function runtime._onInputBegan(input, _gameProcessedEvent)
		if input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.Keyboard then return end
		-- Focus gates. gameProcessedEvent intentionally unused  -  see header comment.
		if wiring.isCapturing and wiring.isCapturing() then return end
		if UserInputService:GetFocusedTextBox() then return end

		-- Hold-leader: leader held + any other key press = dispatch. Pressing the
		-- leader alone does nothing (it's the modifier, not an action). When the
		-- leader is disabled (settings.leaderKey == false), no key is reserved and
		-- the held-check passes unconditionally so any chord keypress dispatches.
		local leaderKC = _currentLeaderKeyCode()
		if leaderKC and input.KeyCode == leaderKC then return end
		if not _isLeaderHeld() then return end
		local combo = _buildComboFromInput(input)
		if not Bindings.isValidCombo(combo) then return end
		local actionId = _index[Bindings.comboKey(combo)]
		if not actionId then return end
		-- When the Shortcuts panel itself is open, only ToggleShortcuts can dispatch  - 
		-- that lets the same shortcut close the panel it just opened. Other actions
		-- are suppressed so chord-tapping inside the panel doesn't accidentally fire
		-- random actions while the user is binding. ToggleUI is also allowlisted so
		-- the user can recover when the panel is open under a hidden ScreenGui
		-- (panel.Visible=true but parent disabled).
		if wiring.isOpen() and actionId ~= "ToggleShortcuts" and actionId ~= "ToggleUI" then return end
		_dispatchActionId(actionId)
	end

	-- Build the index now (Bootstrap calls ensureSettings before us so getSettings returns
	-- a populated table). Hook onChanged so future saves rebuild.
	runtime._rebuildIndex()
	runtime._pushWorkspaceKeys()
	wiring.setOnChanged(function()
		runtime._rebuildIndex()
		runtime._pushWorkspaceKeys()
	end)
	WorkspaceKeys.setGate(wiring.captureHoldsKeys)

	local conn = UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(runtime._onInputBegan)
	if Connections then
		Connections["ShortcutsRuntime"] = conn
	end

	function runtime.stop()
		if conn then conn:Disconnect(); conn = nil end
		wiring.setOnChanged(nil)
		-- The workspace keys stay as they are: Modules/Workspaces runs on without this UI.
		WorkspaceKeys.setGate(nil)
		_index = {}
	end

	return runtime
end

return Runtime

--[[
	Wiring  -  Part-Icles V5 ShortcutKey panel state machine
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle

	Factory: `(deps) -> {open, close, isOpen, populate, ...}`.

	State machine:
	  - Closed: panel.Visible = false. _settings table is the in-memory truth.
	  - Open: visible. populate() rebuilds rows from ctx.Actions filtered by
	    `def.implemented==true`. Search box re-filters live via
	    :GetPropertyChangedSignal("Text").
	  - Capturing: a row's Bind button was clicked. _captureActionId is set, all
	    input is intercepted by the active UIS connection until either (a) Esc
	    cancels, (b) a valid non-modifier-only key fires (with or without
	    modifiers), or (c) any other Bind button is clicked (capture handoff  - 
	    mirrors Studio's keybind UX).

	Save flow (Capture commit):
	  1. New combo built from UIS state.
	  2. Bindings.findOwner(settings, combo, Actions, actionId) → if another action that
	     fires on the same press owns it, warn + drop the previous binding. Conflict
	     policy is "simple override".
	  3. Bindings.assign(settings, actionId, combo). Bindings.save(plugin, _settings).
	  4. populate() rebuilds rows so combo display refreshes for both winner +
	     previous owner.

	Reset:
	  - Two-click confirm. First click flips resetBtn.Text to "Click again to
	    confirm", arms _resetArmed + _resetArmedAt. Second click within
	    _resetConfirmWindow seconds → mod.reset() (Bindings.reset: chords unbound,
	    direct actions back on their defaults; save, populate). No second click →
	    task.delay restores label after window. close() also disarms.

	Direct actions (the workspace keys, `direct = true` in the catalog) are rows like any
	other, shown and captured without the leader. Their keys are read by
	Shortcuts/WorkspaceKeys, which asks captureHoldsKeys() before acting, so the press that
	binds a key does not also run it.

	Settings priming:
	  - mod.ensureSettings() lazy-loads Bindings.load(plugin, Actions) on first
	    access.
	  - Bootstrap calls ensureSettings() right after construction so the runtime
	    (which attaches before any user opens the panel) sees the user's saved
	    bindings on first dispatch.
	  - getSettings() routes through ensureSettings() so it never returns nil.

	NOT user-script-reachable. Internal-only.

	Required deps shape:
	  ctx (must contain ctx.plugin + ctx.Actions),
	  panel = {panel, scrollList, searchBox, resetBtn, headerCloseBtn},
	  Bindings (the storage submodule),
	  Connections (ConnectionManager  -  registers searchBox/resetBtn signals so
	    plugin teardown disconnects them, consistent with every other top-level
	    wiring path),
	  Widgets, Theme.
]]

local Log = require(script.Parent.Parent.Part.Log)

local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

return function(deps)
	local ctx = deps.ctx
	local plugin = ctx.plugin
	local Actions = ctx.Actions
	local panel = deps.panel.panel
	local scrollList = deps.panel.scrollList
	local searchBox = deps.panel.searchBox
	local resetBtn = deps.panel.resetBtn
	local leaderLabel = deps.panel.leaderLabel
	local leaderSetBtn = deps.panel.leaderSetBtn
	local leaderClearBtn = deps.panel.leaderClearBtn
	local Bindings = deps.Bindings
	local Widgets = deps.Widgets
	local Theme = deps.Theme
	local Connections = deps.Connections  -- register signal connections through ConnectionManager

	local W = Widgets
	local T = Theme
	local mod = {}

	local _settings  -- {version, overlayEnabled, bindings}
	local _open = false
	local _captureActionId = nil
	local _captureConn = nil
	-- When the last capture ended. The press that ends a capture reaches the other input
	-- listeners in the same frame, in an order the engine does not promise.
	local _captureEndedAt = -math.huge
	local CAPTURE_SETTLE_SECONDS = 0.1
	-- Forward-declared so _startCapture's mutual-exclusion block can see these as
	-- upvalues. Initialized in the Leader-capture section further down.
	local _leaderCapturing = false
	local _leaderCaptureConn = nil
	local _rows = {}  -- {actionId -> {frame, comboLabel, bindBtn, unbindBtn, applyBtn}}
	local _conflictTimer = nil
	local _destroyed = false
	-- Runtime rebuilds its comboKey reverse-index when bindings change. _onChanged is a
	-- single-callback hook (Runtime.start sets this); fired from every save path (commit
	-- / unbind / reset). Single consumer, so no full Signal needed.
	local _onChanged = nil
	local function _fireChanged()
		if _onChanged then pcall(_onChanged) end
	end
	-- Manual Cmd/Win display preference (NOT OS detection). Roblox plugin API has no
	-- host-OS hook, so Mac vs Win meta-key labeling can't be auto-driven. We read the
	-- plugin setting `DisplayCmdAsMeta` (boolean) at open time; Mac users flip via
	-- `plugin:SetSetting("DisplayCmdAsMeta", true)` in the Studio dev console. Display
	-- labels render "Cmd+" instead of "Win+" for combos with meta=true. open() refreshes
	-- per session so a flip + reopen reflects the label preference immediately. There is
	-- no visible panel toggle yet  -  could surface as a checkbox near Reset if Mac uptake
	-- creates demand.
	local _isMac = false
	local function _refreshIsMac()
		local v = plugin:GetSetting("DisplayCmdAsMeta")
		_isMac = (type(v) == "boolean") and v or false
	end

	-- =========================================================
	-- Capture flow
	-- =========================================================

	-- The leader an action's combo is shown and captured with: none for a direct action.
	local function _leaderFor(actionId)
		if Bindings.isDirect(Actions, actionId) then
			return false
		end
		return Bindings.getLeaderKey(_settings)
	end

	local function _stopCapture(reason)
		if _captureConn then
			_captureConn:Disconnect()
			_captureConn = nil
			_captureEndedAt = os.clock()
		end
		_captureActionId = nil
		-- Restore button labels (populate rebuilds, simpler than per-row state restore).
		mod.populate()
	end

	-- Transient conflict notice {actionId, expiresAt, message}. Populate displays
	-- the message on the affected row's combo label in red until expiresAt.
	local _conflictNotice = nil

	local function _commitCombo(actionId, combo)
		-- _commitCombo can fire with actionId == nil under a race between _stopCapture's
		-- _captureActionId clear and an in-flight InputBegan event. Bail early so format/
		-- warn/save calls never receive nil. The capture flow's caller already gates
		-- re-firing on the boolean return (false → don't _stopCapture again).
		if type(actionId) ~= "string" or actionId == "" then return false end
		if not Bindings.isValidCombo(combo) then return false end
		mod.ensureSettings()
		local owner = Bindings.findOwner(_settings, combo, Actions, actionId)
		if owner and owner ~= actionId then
			Log.warn(("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] %s overrides previous binding %s -> %s"):format(
				tostring(actionId), tostring(owner), Bindings.formatCombo(combo, _isMac, _leaderFor(actionId))))
			Bindings.clear(_settings, Actions, owner)
			-- Stash a transient notice for the row that just lost its binding.
			-- Populate (called from _fireChanged below) will overlay it; another
			-- populate runs after 3s to clear.
			local newName = (Actions[actionId] and Actions[actionId].displayName) or actionId
			_conflictNotice = {
				actionId = owner,
				expiresAt = os.clock() + 3,
				message = "Reassigned to " .. newName,
			}
			if _conflictTimer then pcall(task.cancel, _conflictTimer); _conflictTimer = nil end
			_conflictTimer = task.delay(3, function()
				_conflictTimer = nil
				if _destroyed then return end
				if _conflictNotice and _conflictNotice.actionId == owner then
					_conflictNotice = nil
					mod.populate()
				end
			end)
		end
		Bindings.assign(_settings, actionId, combo)
		Bindings.save(plugin, _settings)
		_fireChanged()
		return true
	end

	local function _startCapture(actionId)
		-- Tear down any existing capture before arming a new one  -  regardless of
		-- whether actionId matches. Otherwise same-row double-click would orphan
		-- the prior listener with its stale captured actionId still alive.
		if _captureConn then _stopCapture("rearm") end
		-- Mutual exclusion with leader capture (defined later in this file). The
		-- next keypress must commit as a chord, not as a new leader. Forward-decl
		-- via _leaderCaptureConn upvalue  -  closure resolves at fire time.
		if _leaderCaptureConn then
			_leaderCaptureConn:Disconnect()
			_leaderCaptureConn = nil
			_leaderCapturing = false
			-- Label refresh happens inline since the leader-row helper isn't visible
			-- to this closure yet. Safe because populate() runs at the end of any
			-- commit path that follows.
			if leaderLabel then
				local lk = Bindings.getLeaderKey(_settings)
				leaderLabel.Text = lk == false and "Leader: (none)" or ("Leader: " .. tostring(lk))
				leaderLabel.TextColor3 = lk == false and T.MutedGold or T.BrightGold
			end
		end
		_captureActionId = actionId
		local row = _rows[actionId]
		if row and row.comboLabel then
			local leaderName = _leaderFor(actionId)
			local hint = leaderName == false
				and "Press key... (Esc cancels)"
				or ("Press key... (hold "..tostring(leaderName).." + key; Esc cancels)")
			row.comboLabel.Text = hint
		end
		-- Bind the actionId in the closure rather than reading the _captureActionId
		-- upvalue at fire time. Otherwise an InputBegan event in flight when
		-- _stopCapture nils the upvalue would pass nil to _commitCombo. Closure
		-- capture pins the value at _startCapture time; _stopCapture's Disconnect
		-- kills the listener but the bound `actionId` survives until that happens.
		local capturingActionId = actionId
		-- InputBegan listener. ProcessEvent passes through Studio bindings  -  we want even
		-- captured-by-Studio combos to commit here, so we listen on InputBegan and check
		-- modifiers via UIS:IsKeyDown rather than relying on the InputObject having them.
		_captureConn = UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input)
			if input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.Keyboard then return end
			-- Bail when a TextBox is focused so typing in the Shortcuts search (or
			-- any other plugin TextBox) doesn't get captured as a chord. Escape is
			-- the exception  -  letting it through lets the user cancel capture
			-- without un-focusing first.
			if input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.Escape then _stopCapture("escape"); return end
			if UserInputService:GetFocusedTextBox() then return end
			-- Leader never lands as the chord key. With hold-leader semantics the user
			-- holds the leader first then taps the chord key; capture must ignore the
			-- leader press so it doesn't bind the leader as the second key. When the
			-- leader is disabled (leaderKey == false), no key is reserved.
			local leaderName = Bindings.getLeaderKey(_settings)
			if leaderName ~= false and input.KeyCode.Name == leaderName then return end
			local kcName = input.KeyCode.Name
			-- Reject modifier-only press; wait for the chord-finishing non-modifier.
			local combo = {
				key = kcName,
				ctrl = UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.LeftControl) or UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.RightControl),
				alt = UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.LeftAlt) or UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.RightAlt),
				shift = UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift) or UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.RightShift),
				meta = false,
			}
			-- Mac meta probe: pcall because LeftMeta enum may not exist on all Studio runtimes.
			pcall(function()
				combo.meta = UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.LeftMeta) or UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.RightMeta)
			end)
			if not Bindings.isValidCombo(combo) then return end  -- modifier-only-key skip
			if _commitCombo(capturingActionId, combo) then _stopCapture("commit") end
		end)
		-- Also register through ConnectionManager so plugin teardown disconnects
		-- the capture listener if the user disables the plugin mid-bind.
		if Connections then Connections["ShortcutsCapture"] = _captureConn end
	end

	-- =========================================================
	-- Leader capture flow
	-- Mirrors chord capture but with KeyCode-only validation (no modifiers).
	-- _leaderCapturing + _leaderCaptureConn are forward-declared near the top so
	-- _startCapture can mutually-exclude with this flow.
	-- =========================================================

	local function _refreshLeaderLabel()
		if not leaderLabel then return end
		local lk = Bindings.getLeaderKey(_settings)
		if lk == false then
			leaderLabel.Text = "Leader: (none)"
			leaderLabel.TextColor3 = T.MutedGold
		else
			leaderLabel.Text = "Leader: " .. tostring(lk)
			leaderLabel.TextColor3 = T.BrightGold
		end
	end

	local function _stopLeaderCapture(_reason)
		if _leaderCaptureConn then
			_leaderCaptureConn:Disconnect()
			_leaderCaptureConn = nil
			_captureEndedAt = os.clock()
		end
		_leaderCapturing = false
		_refreshLeaderLabel()
	end

	-- Reject modifier-only keys at capture time so the picker can't bind LeftShift /
	-- Ctrl / Alt / Meta as a leader (would never produce a "non-leader" keypress).
	local LEADER_MODIFIER_REJECT = {
		LeftControl = true, RightControl = true, LeftAlt = true, RightAlt = true,
		LeftShift = true, RightShift = true, LeftMeta = true, RightMeta = true,
		LeftSuper = true, RightSuper = true,
	}

	local function _startLeaderCapture()
		if _leaderCaptureConn then _stopLeaderCapture("rearm") end
		-- Mutual exclusion with chord capture; otherwise the next keypress would
		-- commit as both a chord binding AND a leader.
		if _captureConn then _stopCapture("leader-rearm") end
		mod.ensureSettings()
		_leaderCapturing = true
		if leaderLabel then
			leaderLabel.Text = "Press leader key... (Esc cancels)"
			leaderLabel.TextColor3 = T.BrightGold
		end
		_leaderCaptureConn = UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input)
			if input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.Keyboard then return end
			if input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.Escape then _stopLeaderCapture("escape"); return end
			if UserInputService:GetFocusedTextBox() then return end
			local kcName = input.KeyCode.Name
			if LEADER_MODIFIER_REJECT[kcName] then return end
			local clean, ok = Bindings.isValidLeader(kcName)
			if not ok then return end
			_settings.leaderKey = clean
			-- A direct action on the new leader's key gives it up.
			Bindings.normalize(_settings, Actions)
			Bindings.save(plugin, _settings)
			_fireChanged()
			_stopLeaderCapture("commit")
			mod.populate()  -- chord display labels refresh with new leader prefix
		end)
		if Connections then Connections["ShortcutsLeaderCapture"] = _leaderCaptureConn end
	end

	local function _clearLeader()
		mod.ensureSettings()
		if _leaderCaptureConn then _stopLeaderCapture("clear") end
		_settings.leaderKey = false
		-- Without a leader a combo has one owner: a chord keeps it over a direct action.
		Bindings.normalize(_settings, Actions)
		Bindings.save(plugin, _settings)
		_fireChanged()
		_refreshLeaderLabel()
		mod.populate()
	end

	-- =========================================================
	-- Row builder
	-- =========================================================

	local function _makeRow(parent, actionId, def, layoutOrder)
		-- Matches UIBuilder convention: Settings panel + Properties rows wrap text in
		-- W.makeBlob (themed background + corner + stroke) and use W.makeLabel for
		-- typography. Plain TextLabels on a transparent row would read as floating
		-- text  -  inconsistent with the rest of the plugin. Row height 24 matches
		-- Settings AERow/USRow.
		local row = Instance.new("Frame")
		row.Name = "Row_" .. actionId
		row.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		row.Size = UDim2.new(1, -4, 0, 24)
		row.LayoutOrder = layoutOrder
		row.Parent = parent

		-- nameBlob fixed at 130px (action names short + bounded). comboBlob fills the
		-- middle minus the right-side button gutter (78px = 22 X + 40 Bind + 16 gaps).
		-- Name blob (left): themed pill with action display name. Internal padding via
		-- UIPadding so text doesn't sit flush against the rounded corner.
		local nameBlob = W.makeBlob("Name", row, UDim2.new(0, 130, 1, -2))
		nameBlob.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 1)
		W.addPadding(nameBlob, 6, 4, 0, 0)
		local nameLabel = W.makeLabel("L", nameBlob, def.displayName or actionId, T.MutedGold, T.Font, 10)
		nameLabel.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
		nameLabel.TextTruncate = Enum.TextTruncate.AtEnd

		-- Combo blob (middle): themed pill showing current binding / suggestion / "(unbound)".
		-- Same treatment as the name blob for visual consistency.
		-- comboBlob right reserve = 208 (74px button gutter) so the bind button sits
		-- close to comboBlob's right edge.
		local comboBlob = W.makeBlob("Combo", row, UDim2.new(1, -208, 1, -2))
		comboBlob.Position = UDim2.new(0, 134, 0, 1)
		W.addPadding(comboBlob, 6, 4, 0, 0)
		local comboLabel = W.makeLabel("L", comboBlob, "(unbound)", T.BrightGold, T.Font, 10)
		comboLabel.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
		comboLabel.TextTruncate = Enum.TextTruncate.AtEnd

		-- Right-anchored buttons. Layout: [...nameBlob...][...comboBlob...] [Bind][X].
		-- Offsets from right edge: X (22) flush at -4; Bind (40) at -(4+22+4)=-30.
		local unbindBtn = W.makeButton("Unbind_"..actionId, row, "X", UDim2.new(0, 22, 1, -4), T.DarkGold)
		unbindBtn.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0)
		unbindBtn.Position = UDim2.new(1, -4, 0, 2)
		unbindBtn.TextSize = 10

		local bindBtn = W.makeButton("Bind_"..actionId, row, "Bind", UDim2.new(0, 40, 1, -4), T.DarkGold)
		bindBtn.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0)
		bindBtn.Position = UDim2.new(1, -30, 0, 2)
		bindBtn.TextSize = 10

		bindBtn.Activated:Connect(function() _startCapture(actionId) end)
		unbindBtn.Activated:Connect(function()
			-- Stop ANY armed capture, not just one matching this row. Clicking X on
			-- a different row while another is in "Press key..." mode would otherwise
			-- leave the original listener alive after populate() destroyed its prompt.
			if _captureConn then _stopCapture("unbind") end
			Bindings.clear(_settings, Actions, actionId)
			Bindings.save(plugin, _settings)
			_fireChanged()
			mod.populate()
		end)

		_rows[actionId] = {
			frame = row, comboLabel = comboLabel,
			bindBtn = bindBtn, unbindBtn = unbindBtn,
		}
		return row
	end

	local function _makeCategoryHeader(parent, name, layoutOrder, text)
		-- Matches BuildProperties section-header style  -  slightly taller, gold accent,
		-- with a small left padding so the label doesn't sit flush.
		local hdr = Instance.new("Frame")
		hdr.Name = "Cat_" .. name
		hdr.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		hdr.Size = UDim2.new(1, -4, 0, 20)
		hdr.LayoutOrder = layoutOrder
		hdr.Parent = parent
		W.addPadding(hdr, 4, 0, 4, 0)
		local lbl = W.makeLabel("L", hdr, text or name, T.Gold, T.Font, 11)
		lbl.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
	end

	-- =========================================================
	-- populate / filter
	-- =========================================================

	function mod.populate()
		-- Clear existing rows + headers (preserve placeholder if no actions; safe to drop it
		-- since populate runs after _settings is loaded).
		for _, child in ipairs(scrollList:GetChildren()) do
			if child:IsA("Frame") or (child:IsA("TextLabel") and child.Name:sub(1,4) == "Cat_") or child.Name == "Placeholder" then
				child:Destroy()
			end
		end
		_rows = {}
		local filter = (searchBox and searchBox.Text or ""):lower()
		-- Group by category, in this order.
		local categoryOrder = {"UI", "Tools", "Edit", "Animate", "Emit", "Editor", "Workspaces"}
		local byCat = {}
		for actionId, def in pairs(Actions) do
			-- Filter to implemented actions only  -  stubs (ResetSelection,
			-- OpenGraphEditor, OpenColorPicker) shouldn't appear in the bindable list.
			if def.implemented == true then
				local matchesFilter = filter == "" or
					(def.displayName or actionId):lower():find(filter, 1, true) ~= nil or
					actionId:lower():find(filter, 1, true) ~= nil
				if matchesFilter then
					local cat = def.category or "Other"
					byCat[cat] = byCat[cat] or {}
					table.insert(byCat[cat], {actionId = actionId, def = def})
				end
			end
		end
		local layoutOrder = 0
		for _, cat in ipairs(categoryOrder) do
			local rows = byCat[cat]
			if rows and #rows > 0 then
				-- A category of direct actions says so: its rows show a key without the leader.
				local headerText = cat
				if rows[1].def.direct then
					headerText = cat .. "  (key alone, no leader)"
				end
				_makeCategoryHeader(scrollList, cat, layoutOrder, headerText); layoutOrder = layoutOrder + 1
				-- Stable per-category order: alphabetical actionId.
				table.sort(rows, function(a, b) return a.actionId < b.actionId end)
				for _, entry in ipairs(rows) do
					_makeRow(scrollList, entry.actionId, entry.def, layoutOrder)
					-- Refresh combo label. Unbound rows read "(unbound)"; bound rows show
					-- the actual combo. An active conflict notice for this row overlays a
					-- red message instead.
					local combo = _settings.bindings[entry.actionId]
					local cl = _rows[entry.actionId].comboLabel
					if _conflictNotice and _conflictNotice.actionId == entry.actionId and os.clock() < _conflictNotice.expiresAt then
						cl.Text = _conflictNotice.message
						cl.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(220, 80, 80)
					else
						cl.Text = combo and Bindings.formatCombo(combo, _isMac, _leaderFor(entry.actionId)) or "(unbound)"
						cl.TextColor3 = T.MutedGold
					end
					layoutOrder = layoutOrder + 1
				end
			end
		end
	end

	-- =========================================================
	-- ensureSettings / Reset / open / close
	-- =========================================================

	-- Runtime attaches at plugin setup BEFORE the user has opened the panel.
	-- getSettings() must return a populated table, so prime _settings lazily on
	-- first access instead of at open() time.
	function mod.ensureSettings()
		if _settings == nil then
			-- Defense-in-depth: Bindings.load already normalizes the version field,
			-- but any other unforeseen error inside load() must NOT abort plugin
			-- bootstrap. Fall back to defaults on any error.
			local ok, result = pcall(Bindings.load, plugin, Actions)
			if ok and type(result) == "table" then
				_settings = result
			else
				Log.warn("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] Bindings.load failed; using defaults: "..tostring(result))
				_settings = {version = Bindings.VERSION, overlayEnabled = true, bindings = Bindings._copyDefaults(), unbound = {}}
				pcall(Bindings.normalize, _settings, Actions)
			end
		end
		return _settings
	end

	-- Two-click reset confirm. First click flips the button to a confirm state; the
	-- second click within `_resetConfirmWindow` seconds commits. Auto-reverts after
	-- the window with task.delay.
	local _resetArmed = false
	local _resetArmedAt = 0
	local _resetConfirmWindow = 3
	local _resetOriginalText = resetBtn and resetBtn.Text or "Reset all"
	local function _disarmReset()
		_resetArmed = false
		if resetBtn then resetBtn.Text = _resetOriginalText end
	end
	function mod.reset()
		mod.ensureSettings()
		Bindings.reset(_settings, Actions)
		Bindings.save(plugin, _settings)
		_disarmReset()
		-- Tear down any armed capture so a post-reset keypress doesn't silently
		-- rebind a row the user just told us to clear.
		if _captureConn then _stopCapture("reset") end
		_fireChanged()
		mod.populate()
	end
	local function _onResetClick()
		if not _open then return end
		if _resetArmed and (os.clock() - _resetArmedAt) <= _resetConfirmWindow then
			mod.reset()
			return
		end
		_resetArmed = true
		_resetArmedAt = os.clock()
		if resetBtn then resetBtn.Text = "Click again to confirm" end
		task.delay(_resetConfirmWindow, function()
			-- Bail if the user already clicked through. Otherwise restore label.
			if _resetArmed and (os.clock() - _resetArmedAt) >= _resetConfirmWindow - 0.05 then
				_disarmReset()
			end
		end)
	end

	function mod.open()
		if _open then return end
		_open = true
		mod.ensureSettings()
		_refreshIsMac()  -- re-read plugin setting so label preference picks up flips.
		_refreshLeaderLabel()
		panel.Visible = true
		mod.populate()
	end

	function mod.close()
		if not _open then return end
		_open = false
		_stopCapture("close")
		_stopLeaderCapture("close")
		_disarmReset()
		panel.Visible = false
	end

	-- Plugin-teardown hook; cancels pending conflict-notice timer + an in-flight
	-- capture's InputBegan listener (otherwise the disconnect-on-stop path never runs
	-- when the user toggles plugin off mid-capture, leaving an orphan Connection).
	function mod.destroy()
		_destroyed = true
		if _captureConn then _captureConn:Disconnect(); _captureConn = nil end
		_captureActionId = nil
		if _leaderCaptureConn then _leaderCaptureConn:Disconnect(); _leaderCaptureConn = nil end
		_leaderCapturing = false
		if _conflictTimer then pcall(task.cancel, _conflictTimer); _conflictTimer = nil end
		_conflictNotice = nil
	end

	function mod.isOpen() return _open end
	function mod.isCapturing() return _captureActionId ~= nil or _leaderCapturing end

	-- True while a key press belongs to a capture: one is armed, or one just ended.
	function mod.captureHoldsKeys()
		if mod.isCapturing() then
			return true
		end
		return os.clock() - _captureEndedAt < CAPTURE_SETTLE_SECONDS
	end

	function mod.getSettings()
		-- Runtime safety: if dispatcher loads before user opens the panel, prime defaults so
		-- the 3 pre-bound shortcuts still fire on first install.
		return mod.ensureSettings()
	end

	-- Runtime registers a callback here; Wiring fires it after every save (commit /
	-- unbind / reset) so the reverse-index rebuilds. Single-consumer hook  -  replace
	-- with a Signal if a second consumer ever needs it.
	function mod.setOnChanged(callback)
		_onChanged = callback
	end

	-- Register signal connections through ConnectionManager so plugin teardown
	-- disconnects them (consistent with every other top-level wiring path).
	if Connections then
		if searchBox then
			Connections["ShortcutsSearchChanged"] = searchBox:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Text"):Connect(function()
				if _open then mod.populate() end
			end)
		end
		if resetBtn then
			Connections["ShortcutsReset"] = resetBtn.Activated:Connect(_onResetClick)
		end
		if leaderSetBtn then
			Connections["ShortcutsLeaderSet"] = leaderSetBtn.Activated:Connect(_startLeaderCapture)
		end
		if leaderClearBtn then
			Connections["ShortcutsLeaderClear"] = leaderClearBtn.Activated:Connect(_clearLeader)
		end
	else
		-- Defensive fallback if Bootstrap forgets to pass Connections. Module is plugin-lifetime
		-- so leak risk is small but warn so the gap surfaces in dev.
		Log.warn("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] Wiring built without Connections  -  search/reset signals are dangling")
		if searchBox then searchBox:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Text"):Connect(function() if _open then mod.populate() end end) end
		if resetBtn then resetBtn.Activated:Connect(_onResetClick) end
		if leaderSetBtn then leaderSetBtn.Activated:Connect(_startLeaderCapture) end
		if leaderClearBtn then leaderClearBtn.Activated:Connect(_clearLeader) end
	end

	return mod
end

--[[
	WorkspaceKeys  -  which key does what in Modules/Workspaces: the bindings, and the test of a
	key press against them.
	  WorkspaceKeys.DEFAULTS            { next, send, new, merge, bar } -> combo
	  WorkspaceKeys.set(combos, leader) combos: the same names -> combo, a name left out is
	                                    unbound; leader: KeyCode name of the shortcut leader, or false
	  WorkspaceKeys.setGate(isBlocked)  a function that returns true while the keys must not act
	                                    (a shortcut is being captured); nil clears it
	  WorkspaceKeys.match(input) -> name or nil
	A combo is { key = KeyCode name, ctrl, alt, shift, meta }, as Shortcuts/Bindings stores it.
	Matching: a press that equals a combo exactly wins. Otherwise a combo without modifiers also
	takes the press with Shift held, as long as Ctrl, Alt and Meta are up and the key is not a
	letter: "=" and "+" are one key. The keypad's plus and minus count as "=" and "-".
	Nothing acts while the leader is held (another shortcut is in progress) or a TextBox has focus.
	Cross-file invariants: Modules/Workspaces calls match() from its own input listener, which
	keeps running while the plugin's UI is toggled off, so the bindings set here outlive the UI.
	Shortcuts/Runtime calls set() on every setup and after every change in the Shortcuts panel;
	the names are the `workspaceKey` fields of the Workspace actions in Modules/Actions.
]]

local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

local function combo(key, shift)
	return { key = key, ctrl = false, alt = false, shift = shift == true, meta = false }
end

local ALIASES = { KeypadPlus = "Equals", KeypadMinus = "Minus" }

local WorkspaceKeys = {}

WorkspaceKeys.DEFAULTS = {
	next = combo("Slash"),
	send = combo("Slash", true),
	new = combo("Equals"),
	merge = combo("Minus"),
	bar = combo("H"),
}

local combos = WorkspaceKeys.DEFAULTS
local leader = nil
local gate = nil

-- Enum.KeyCode raises on a name it does not have (LeftMeta is missing on some runtimes).
local function keyCode(name)
	local found, code = pcall(function()
		return Enum.KeyCode[name]
	end)
	if found then
		return code
	end
	return nil
end

local function eitherDown(leftName, rightName)
	local left = keyCode(leftName)
	local right = keyCode(rightName)
	if left and UserInputService:IsKeyDown(left) then
		return true
	end
	return right ~= nil and UserInputService:IsKeyDown(right)
end

function WorkspaceKeys.set(newCombos, leaderName)
	combos = newCombos
	leader = nil
	if type(leaderName) == "string" then
		leader = keyCode(leaderName)
	end
end

function WorkspaceKeys.setGate(isBlocked)
	gate = isBlocked
end

function WorkspaceKeys.match(input)
	if input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.Keyboard then
		return nil
	end
	if UserInputService:GetFocusedTextBox() then
		return nil
	end
	if gate and gate() then
		return nil
	end
	if leader and UserInputService:IsKeyDown(leader) then
		return nil
	end

	local key = ALIASES[input.KeyCode.Name] or input.KeyCode.Name
	local ctrl = eitherDown("LeftControl", "RightControl")
	local alt = eitherDown("LeftAlt", "RightAlt")
	local shift = eitherDown("LeftShift", "RightShift")
	local meta = eitherDown("LeftMeta", "RightMeta")
	-- Letter keys are named by one character; Shift with a letter is a different shortcut.
	local shiftIsSameKey = #key > 1 and not (ctrl or alt or meta)

	local loose = nil
	for name, bound in pairs(combos) do
		if bound.key == key then
			if bound.ctrl == ctrl and bound.alt == alt and bound.shift == shift and bound.meta == meta then
				return name
			end
			local bare = not (bound.ctrl or bound.alt or bound.shift or bound.meta)
			if bare and shiftIsSameKey then
				loose = name
			end
		end
	end
	return loose
end

return WorkspaceKeys

-- task.wait between requires spreads obfuscated VM bootstrap across frames so the
-- initial UIBuilder load doesn't pile onto the same frame as Part's mixin chain.
local C = require(script.Constants); task.wait()
local W = require(script.Widgets); task.wait()
local Workspaces = require(script.Parent.Workspaces)

local buildToolbar = require(script.BuildToolbar)

-- BUILD (orchestrator)
-- Builds the whole UI, a few milliseconds per frame (BuildPacer), and shows it when done.
-- Returns nil when teardown cancelled the build; its half-built ScreenGui is removed.
function UIBuilder:Build(TypeRegistry)
	local started = os.clock()
	local build = BuildPacer.begin()
	local ok, result = xpcall(self._buildAll, debug.traceback, self, TypeRegistry)
	BuildPacer.finish(build)
	if ok and not build.cancelled then
		Log.print(string.format("[Part-Icles] UI built in %.2f s over %d frames", os.clock() - started, build.frames))
		return result
	end
	if build.screenGui then build.screenGui:Destroy() end
	if build.cancelled then return nil end
	error(result, 0)
end

function UIBuilder:_buildAll(TypeRegistry)
	-- Reset widget tracking
	W.reset()
	-- Widgets read colours and metrics at build time, so derive them from the saved theme first.
	C.refresh()
	for _, old in pairs(game:GetService('CoreGui'):GetChildren()) do
		if old:IsA("ScreenGui") and old.Name == "PartIclesUI" then old:Destroy() end
	end
	local sg = Instance.new("ScreenGui"); sg.Name = "PartIclesUI"; sg.ZIndexBehavior = Enum.ZIndexBehavior.Sibling
	sg.ResetOnSpawn = false; sg.Enabled = false; sg.Parent = game:GetService('CoreGui')
	UIBuilder._screenGui = sg
	BuildPacer.claim(sg)
	TypeScale.watch(sg)
	-- Hand the ScreenGui to the toast system so showToast can parent its frames.
	if W.setToastParent then W.setToastParent(sg) end
	-- The panel last pressed or opened draws on top (PanelStack). It stacks top-level frames with
	-- a ZIndex under 20; popups and modals built here keep theirs at 20 or above.
	W.watchPanelStack(sg)
	local uiScale = Instance.new("UIScale"); uiScale.Scale = C.DEFAULT_UI_SCALE_PERCENT / 100 * C.BASE_UI_SCALE; uiScale.Parent = sg

	local hudRefs = buildHUD(sg)
	W.makeTray(hudRefs.HUD)
	-- The workspace bar lives outside this ScreenGui; it repaints with every theme change.
	table.insert(W.getThemed().repaints, Workspaces.refreshTheme)
	local propRefs = BP.buildProperties(sg)
	local settingsRefs = buildSettings(sg)
	local toolbar = buildToolbar(sg)
	local counter, counterLabel = toolbar.counter, toolbar.counterLabel
	local optIndicator, optLabel = toolbar.optIndicator, toolbar.optLabel
	local toggleRefs = toolbar.toggles
	-- The Classic tool layouts or the ones for the other modes, with the same refs either way.
	local toolBuilders = TP.builders()
	local qMenuRefs = toolBuilders.buildQMenu(sg)
	local deckRefs = TD.build(sg, TypeRegistry)
	local hueRefs = toolBuilders.buildHueChanger(sg)
	local emitCodeRefs = toolBuilders.buildEmitCode(sg)
	local fixRefs = toolBuilders.buildFixBanner(sg)
	local themeRefs = buildThemeEditor(sg)
	local dotsMenuRefs = W.buildDotsMenu(sg)
	local inventoryRefs = IP.build(sg)
	-- Randomizer modal panel. Wiring + button handlers attached in init.server.lua
	-- because RandomizerWiring needs ctx-bound deps. Refs merge into `ui` below
	-- (panel + buttons + headerCloseBtn referenced by name from init.server.lua).
	local RandomizerPanel = require(script.RandomizerPanel)
	local randomizerRefs = RandomizerPanel.build(sg)
	-- Re-key under "Randomizer" prefix to avoid clashing with QMenu's "Randomize" Activated button.
	local randomizerUI = {
		RandomizerPanel = randomizerRefs.panel,
		RandomizerSectionList = randomizerRefs.sectionList,
		RandomizerRollAllBtn = randomizerRefs.rollAllBtn,
		RandomizerApplyBtn = randomizerRefs.applyBtn,
		RandomizerCancelBtn = randomizerRefs.cancelBtn,
		RandomizerHeaderCloseBtn = randomizerRefs.headerCloseBtn,
	}
	-- ShortcutPanel modal. Bootstrap (Modules/Shortcuts) wires the Settings panel
	-- "Shortcuts" button to wiring.open/close, and panel headerCloseBtn to close().
	local ShortcutPanel = require(script.ShortcutPanel)
	local shortcutRefs = ShortcutPanel.build(sg)
	local shortcutUI = {
		ShortcutPanel = shortcutRefs.panel,
		ShortcutsList = shortcutRefs.scrollList,
		ShortcutsSearch = shortcutRefs.searchBox,
		ShortcutsReset = shortcutRefs.resetBtn,
		ShortcutsHeaderClose = shortcutRefs.headerCloseBtn,
		ShortcutsLeaderLabel = shortcutRefs.leaderLabel,
		ShortcutsLeaderSet = shortcutRefs.leaderSetBtn,
		ShortcutsLeaderClear = shortcutRefs.leaderClearBtn,
	}

	-- Default positions: [Re:][PropertyTools][Properties] left to right, Hue and Emit Code bottom-left.
	local dockGap = 6
	local toolsWidth = deckRefs.PropertyToolsDeck.Size.X.Offset
	local reWidth = deckRefs.ReDeck.Size.X.Offset
	local col1 = -(LAYOUT.PropsX + dockGap + toolsWidth)
	local col2 = -(LAYOUT.PropsX + dockGap + toolsWidth + dockGap + reWidth)
	local hueSize = hueRefs.HuePanel.Size
	local bottomGap = 40
	local defaultPositions = {
		[deckRefs.PropertyToolsDeck]    = UDim2.new(1, col1, 0, LAYOUT.PropsY),
		[deckRefs.ReDeck]               = UDim2.new(1, col2, 0, LAYOUT.PropsY),
		[hueRefs.HuePanel]             = UDim2.new(0, 12, 1, -(hueSize.Y.Offset + bottomGap)),
		[emitCodeRefs.EmitCodePanel]    = UDim2.new(0, 12 + hueSize.X.Offset + 8, 1, -(emitCodeRefs.EmitCodePanel.Size.Y.Offset + bottomGap)),
		-- RandomizerPanel and ShortcutPanel: centered modals (_noSnap). W.makeToolPanel sets no
		-- default Position, so a _noSnap panel needs an explicit entry here or it pins to top-left.
		[randomizerRefs.panel]          = UDim2.new(0.5, -randomizerRefs.panel.Size.X.Offset / 2, 0.5, -randomizerRefs.panel.Size.Y.Offset / 2),
		[shortcutRefs.panel]            = UDim2.new(0.5, -shortcutRefs.panel.Size.X.Offset / 2, 0.5, -shortcutRefs.panel.Size.Y.Offset / 2),
	}

	-- The Tools menu's builder places it; Reset Layout returns it there.
	local toolsMenuHome = qMenuRefs.QMenu.Position

	-- Record original sizes for reset
	local defaultSizes = {}
	for panel, pos in pairs(defaultPositions) do
		panel.Position = pos; defaultSizes[panel] = panel.Size
	end
	defaultSizes[inventoryRefs.InventoryPanel] = inventoryRefs.InventoryPanel.Size
	-- From here on Properties and the Inventory give way to a panel opened or moved over them
	-- (PanelPush): every panel has its place.
	W.watchPanelPush(sg)

	-- Register panels for magnetic snap
	W.registerPanel(hudRefs.HUD)
	W.registerPanel(propRefs.PropsPanel)
	W.registerPanel(settingsRefs.SettingsPanel)
	W.registerPanel(qMenuRefs.QMenu)
	W.registerPanel(deckRefs.ReDeck)
	W.registerPanel(deckRefs.PropertyToolsDeck)
	W.registerPanel(hueRefs.HuePanel)
	-- Selection tools fold into the HUD tray while nothing is selected (SelectionHandler calls autoTidy).
	W.registerTidyPanel(deckRefs.ReDeck)
	W.registerTidyPanel(deckRefs.PropertyToolsDeck)
	W.registerTidyPanel(hueRefs.HuePanel)
	W.registerPanel(inventoryRefs.InventoryPanel)
	-- Outside Classic the details are a bar inside the inventory panel, not a panel of their own.
	if inventoryRefs.InvDetail and inventoryRefs.InvDetail.Parent == sg then W.registerPanel(inventoryRefs.InvDetail) end

	-- Layout reset
	local function resetLayout()
		-- Positions are set outright below: a pushed panel goes back to its own place first (PanelPush).
		W.releasePushes()
		for panel, pos in pairs(defaultPositions) do panel.Position = pos end
		for panel, size in pairs(defaultSizes) do panel.Size = size end
		hudRefs.HUD.Position = UDim2.new(0, LAYOUT.HudX, 0, LAYOUT.HudY)
		propRefs.PropsPanel.Position = UDim2.new(1, -LAYOUT.PropsX, 0, LAYOUT.PropsY)
		qMenuRefs.QMenu.Position = toolsMenuHome
		inventoryRefs.InventoryPanel.Position = inventoryRefs.InvHome or UDim2.new(0.5, -240, 0.2, 0)
		if inventoryRefs.InvDetail then inventoryRefs.InvDetail.Visible = false end
		if inventoryRefs.InvImportDialog then inventoryRefs.InvImportDialog.Visible = false end
		if inventoryRefs.InvAddDialog then inventoryRefs.InvAddDialog.Visible = false end
	end

	-- Wire toggles (HUD/Props close buttons wired in QOLWiring where ctx is available)
	local function dimToggle(btn, panel)
		btn.Activated:Connect(function() panel.Visible = not panel.Visible end)
	end
	-- A toggle that stands for a panel is lit exactly while that panel is visible, however it
	-- was shown or hidden (click, close button, shortcut, saved layout, tray, Reset Layout).
	local function followPanel(btn, panel)
		toggleRefs.set(btn, panel.Visible)
		panel:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Visible"):Connect(function()
			toggleRefs.set(btn, panel.Visible)
		end)
	end
	followPanel(toggleRefs.counterToggle, counter)
	followPanel(toggleRefs.qolToggle, qMenuRefs.QMenu)
	followPanel(toggleRefs.settingsToggle, settingsRefs.SettingsPanel)
	followPanel(toggleRefs.inventoryToggle, inventoryRefs.InventoryPanel)
	-- Settings toolbar toggle: wired to toolToggles.toggleSettings below so click + Action
	-- share one path.
	settingsRefs.SettingsClose.Activated:Connect(function() settingsRefs.SettingsPanel.Visible = false end)
	dimToggle(toggleRefs.counterToggle, counter)
	dimToggle(toggleRefs.qolToggle, qMenuRefs.QMenu)

	-- Tool-toggle helpers extracted so both QMenu Activated and Actions shortcut
	-- handlers go through the same path (deck tabs + deferred resolveOverlap +
	-- Settings color sync). Exposed via the returned `ui` table.
	local function _toggleSolo(panel)
		panel.Visible = not panel.Visible
		if panel.Visible then task.defer(function() W.resolveOverlap(panel) end) end
	end
	local toolToggles = {
		toggleResize    = function() deckRefs.ReDeckApi.toggle("Size") end,
		toggleRetime    = function() deckRefs.ReDeckApi.toggle("Time") end,
		toggleReDeck    = function() deckRefs.ReDeckApi.toggle() end,
		toggleClipboard = function() deckRefs.PropertyToolsDeckApi.toggle("Clipboard") end,
		toggleShifter   = function() deckRefs.PropertyToolsDeckApi.toggle("Shifter") end,
		togglePropertyTools = function() deckRefs.PropertyToolsDeckApi.toggle() end,
		toggleHue       = function() _toggleSolo(hueRefs.HuePanel) end,
		toggleEmitCode  = function() _toggleSolo(emitCodeRefs.EmitCodePanel) end,
		toggleSettings  = function()
			settingsRefs.SettingsPanel.Visible = not settingsRefs.SettingsPanel.Visible
		end,
	}
	qMenuRefs.ReSizeTime.Activated:Connect(toolToggles.toggleReDeck)
	qMenuRefs.Hue.Activated:Connect(toolToggles.toggleHue)
	qMenuRefs.PropertyTools.Activated:Connect(toolToggles.togglePropertyTools)
	qMenuRefs.EmitCode.Activated:Connect(toolToggles.toggleEmitCode)
	toggleRefs.settingsToggle.Activated:Connect(toolToggles.toggleSettings)
	settingsRefs.ResetLayout = resetLayout

	if settingsRefs.EditThemeButton then
		settingsRefs.EditThemeButton.Activated:Connect(function()
			themeRefs.ThemeEditor.Visible = true
		end)
	end

	local ui = {}
	for _, tbl in ipairs({hudRefs, propRefs, settingsRefs, qMenuRefs, deckRefs, hueRefs, emitCodeRefs, fixRefs, themeRefs, dotsMenuRefs, inventoryRefs, randomizerUI, shortcutUI}) do
		for k, v in pairs(tbl) do ui[k] = v end
	end
	sg.Enabled = true -- Show UI only after everything is built (prevents partial flash under obfuscation)
	ui.ScreenGui = sg; ui.UIScale = uiScale; ui.Counter = counter; ui.CounterLabel = counterLabel
	ui.OptIndicator = optIndicator; ui.OptLabel = optLabel; ui.Toggles = toggleRefs
	-- Tool-toggle helpers exposed so shortcut Actions can mirror toolbar behavior.
	for k, v in pairs(toolToggles) do ui[k] = v end
	ui.autoTidy = W.autoTidy
	return ui
end

-- The auto-emit icon is green while auto-emit runs. Its tint is repainted from the theme after
-- a theme change: ThemeApply never matches image tints by colour.
local function wireAutoEmitIcon(refs, icon)
	local lit = false
	local function paintIcon()
		icon.ImageColor3 = lit and T.Green or T.MutedGold
	end
	function refs.setAutoEmitLit(on)
		lit = on
		paintIcon()
	end
	table.insert(W.getThemed().repaints, paintIcon)
	paintIcon()
end

--[[
	BuildPacer  -  spreads the startup UI build over frames.

	UIBuilder:Build marks its thread as a paced build. Builders call step() as they go; on the
	paced thread step() hands the frame back to Studio once the build has run for
	BUDGET_SECONDS, so the build never holds Studio for longer than that. On any other thread
	step() does nothing, so the same builders stay synchronous when they run later (a list
	refresh, a rebuilt row).

	BuildPacer.begin() -> build       on the thread that builds; build = { frames, cancelled, screenGui }
	BuildPacer.claim(screenGui)       the ScreenGui this thread's build is filling (removed on cancel)
	BuildPacer.step()
	BuildPacer.finish(build)          the thread stops being paced
	BuildPacer.cancelAll()            every build in flight stops at its next step (teardown)

	A cancelled build raises BuildPacer.CANCELLED from step(); UIBuilder:Build catches it.
]]

local BuildPacer = {}

BuildPacer.CANCELLED = "Part-Icles UI build cancelled"
-- Building time per frame. Studio keeps the rest of a 60 fps frame for itself.
local BUDGET_SECONDS = 0.008

local builds = {}

function BuildPacer.begin()
	local build = { frames = 0, cancelled = false, screenGui = nil, sliceStart = os.clock() }
	builds[coroutine.running()] = build
	return build
end

function BuildPacer.claim(screenGui)
	local build = builds[coroutine.running()]
	if build then build.screenGui = screenGui end
end

function BuildPacer.step()
	local build = builds[coroutine.running()]
	if not build or os.clock() - build.sliceStart < BUDGET_SECONDS then return end
	task.wait()
	build.frames += 1
	build.sliceStart = os.clock()
	if build.cancelled then error(BuildPacer.CANCELLED, 0) end
end

function BuildPacer.finish(build)
	for thread, entry in pairs(builds) do
		if entry == build then builds[thread] = nil end
	end
end

function BuildPacer.cancelAll()
	for _, build in pairs(builds) do
		build.cancelled = true
	end
end

return BuildPacer

function BuildPropertiesContainer.buildSection(scroll, refs)
	-- A row with this config gets an asterisk that opens "Apply to": the kinds of thing the
	-- property acts on (TypeDataContainer.APPLY_KINDS; PropertyInputsContainer wires it). The
	-- two light rows have none: only particle emitters have those properties.
	local applyTo = { kind = "apply-to", kinds = { "Emitter", "Mesh" } }
	local containerDefs = {
		{name = "Emission", rows = {
			{key="Enabled",  label="Enabled", type="toggle"},
			{key="EmitMode", label="Type", type="dropdown", options={"Auto","Burst"}, default="Auto"},
			{key="Rate",     label="Rate", type="input", default="2"},
			{key="Lifetime", label="Lifetime", type="input", default="1, 1", placeholder="min, max"},
			-- The options are TypeDataContainer.MODES: the runtime compares the stored text.
			{key="Mode",     label="Mode", type="dropdown", options={"Absolute","Relative","Relative Lifetime","Relative Span"}, default="Absolute"},
		}},

local function buildModern(screenGui)

	panel.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 1)

	refs.UIScaleBox = W.makeNumberRow(panel, "UIScale", "UI Scale %", tostring(C.DEFAULT_UI_SCALE_PERCENT), labelWidth, 2)

	refs.ParticleCapBox = W.makeNumberRow(panel, "ParticleCap", "Particle Cap", "1000", labelWidth, 3)

	refs.AutoUpdateToggle = W.makeSwitchRow(panel, "AutoUpdate", "Auto-Update", 5)

	workspacesLabel.TextTruncate = Enum.TextTruncate.AtEnd

	W.makeDivider(panel, 9)

	refs.EditThemeButton = W.makeActionButton(panel, "EditTheme", "Edit Theme", 10)
	refs.ShortcutsButton = W.makeActionButton(panel, "Shortcuts", "Shortcuts", 11)
	refs.ResetLayoutButton = W.makeActionButton(panel, "ResetLayout", "Reset Layout", 12)
	-- QOLWiring swaps this label to "Checking..." while a check runs.

	refs.SettingsPanel = panel
	return refs
end

return function(screenGui)
	if C.MODE.Structure.Classic then
		return buildClassic(screenGui)
	end
	return buildModern(screenGui)
end

--[[
	BuildThemeEditor  -  the theme editor: mode and text size, the six theme colours, title font,
	background image, preset, theme code, and Apply / Cancel / Reset.
	Returns build(screenGui) -> refs: ThemeEditor, ModeDropdown, ModeOnChanged, AccentColor,
	BgColor, BlobColor, SliderColor, ScrollBarColor, TextColor (each { hex, swatch }), BgImageBox,
	BgImageOpacityBox, FontDropdown, FontDropdownOnChanged, PresetDropdownLbl, PresetOnChanged,
	ThemeCodeBox, ExportTheme, ImportTheme, ApplyTheme, CancelTheme, ResetTheme; Classic adds
	PanelOpacityBox and BlobOpacityBox, the other modes TextSizeDropdown and TextSizeOnChanged.
	ThemeWiring fills and reads them by name. A mode or text-size change takes effect on Apply,
	which rebuilds the UI. Classic keeps the original layout; the other modes use the shared
	panel chrome.
]]

	-- Mode and text size change sizes as well as colours, so ThemeWiring rebuilds the UI on Apply.

-- Side of the square colour swatch in a colour row.
local SWATCH = 20

local function buildModern(screenGui)
	local sizes = PanelSizes.get()
	local labelWidth = sizes.ThemeEditorLabel
	local valueOffset = labelWidth + LAYOUT.LabelGap
	local refs = {}

	local panel = W.makePanel(screenGui, "ThemeEditor", sizes.ThemeEditor)
	panel.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, -sizes.ThemeEditor / 2, 0, 24)
	panel.ZIndex = 5
	panel.Visible = false

	-- Cancel closes the editor: it also puts back the theme being previewed.
	local bar = W.makeTitleBar(panel, "Theme Editor", 0)
	bar.close:Destroy()
	bar.title.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0)
	bar.dragHandle.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0)
	W.makeDraggable(panel, bar.dragHandle)

	-- Label on the left, a dropdown filling the rest.
	local function makeChoiceRow(name, label, order, options, current)
		local row = W.makeRowFrame(panel, name .. "Row", order)
		W.makeRowLabel(row, label, labelWidth)
		local valueLabel, wrap, onChanged = W.makeDropdown(name .. "Dropdown", row, options, current)
		wrap.Position = UDim2.new(0, valueOffset, 0, 0)
		wrap.Size = UDim2.new(1, -valueOffset, 1, 0)
		return valueLabel, onChanged
	end

	-- Label, a swatch that opens the colour picker, and the colour's hex code.
	local function makeColorRow(name, label, order, color)
		local row = W.makeRowFrame(panel, name .. "Row", order)
		W.makeRowLabel(row, label, labelWidth)

		local swatch = Instance.new("TextButton")
		swatch.Name = "Swatch"
		swatch.Text = ""
		swatch.AutoButtonColor = false
		swatch.BorderSizePixel = 0
		swatch.BackgroundColor3 = color
		swatch.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0, 0.5)
		swatch.Position = UDim2.new(0, valueOffset, 0.5, 0)
		swatch.Size = UDim2.new(0, SWATCH, 0, SWATCH)
		-- A user colour: the theme's colour-matching pass must not repaint it.
		swatch:SetAttribute("_noColorRemap", true)
		swatch.Parent = row
		W.addCorner(swatch)
		W.addStroke(swatch)

		local hexOffset = valueOffset + SWATCH + LAYOUT.LabelGap
		local hex, field = W.makeTextField(row, name, C.color3ToHex(color), Enum.TextXAlignment.Left)
		field.Position = UDim2.new(0, hexOffset, 0, 0)
		field.Size = UDim2.new(1, -hexOffset, 1, 0)
		return { hex = hex, swatch = swatch }
	end

	local sizeNames = {}
	for _, size in ipairs(ThemeModes.TEXT_SIZES) do
		table.insert(sizeNames, tostring(size))
	end
	refs.ModeDropdown, refs.ModeOnChanged = makeChoiceRow("Mode", "Mode", 1, ThemeModes.ORDER, T.Mode)
	refs.TextSizeDropdown, refs.TextSizeOnChanged = makeChoiceRow("TextSize", "Text size", 2, sizeNames, tostring(T.TextSize))
	local presetNames = { "Custom" }
	for _, preset in ipairs(C.THEME_PRESETS) do
		table.insert(presetNames, preset.name)
	end
	refs.PresetDropdownLbl, refs.PresetOnChanged = makeChoiceRow("Preset", "Preset", 3, presetNames, "Custom")

	W.makeDivider(panel, 4)

	refs.AccentColor = makeColorRow("Accent", "Accent", 5, T.InputAccent)
	refs.BgColor = makeColorRow("Background", "Background", 6, T.InputBg)
	refs.BlobColor = makeColorRow("Field", "Field", 7, T.InputBlob)

--[[
	BuildToolbar  -  the bottom edge of the screen: the particle counter and the optimization
	indicator on the left, the menu button and its strip of panel toggles on the right.
	Returns build(screenGui) -> { counter, counterLabel, optIndicator, optLabel, toggles }, where
	toggles = { emitToggle, propsToggle, counterToggle, qolToggle, settingsToggle, inventoryToggle,
	motionToggle, bar, menuBtn, strip, set }.
	toggles.set(button, on) is the one way a toggle is lit or dimmed. Wiring calls it for the
	toggles that stand for a setting (Emit, Properties, Motion); UIBuilder binds the ones that
	stand for a panel (Counter, Tools, Settings, Inventory) to that panel's Visible, so they
	cannot drift from what is on screen. Every toggle starts dimmed until one of the two sets it.
	Wiring also writes the counter and indicator texts, and shows or hides the two boxes.
	Classic keeps the original layout and lights a toggle through its text colour; the other
	modes use the segmented strip the Inventory's tabs use (WidgetSegments), lit softly and in
	the panels' colour, and size the bar by the theme's row height (PanelSizes.bottomBarTop gives
	panels above it the bar's top).
]]

local C = require(script.Parent.Constants)
local W = require(script.Parent.Widgets)
local TypeScale = require(script.Parent.TypeScale)
local PanelSizes = require(script.Parent.PanelSizes)

local function buildOptIndicator(sg)

local function buildToggles(sg)
	local bar = Instance.new("Frame"); bar.Name = "ToggleBar"; bar.BackgroundTransparency = 1

	sl.SortOrder = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder; sl.HorizontalAlignment = Enum.HorizontalAlignment.Right

		b.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.X; b.TextSize = 9; b.LayoutOrder = lo
		local p = Instance.new("UIPadding"); p.PaddingLeft = UDim.new(0,6); p.PaddingRight = UDim.new(0,6); p.Parent = b

	local eb = makeStripBtn("EmitToggle", "Emit", T.DarkGold, 0)

local function buildClassic(sg)
